The highest-paid knowledge workers in 2028 may not be doing the work. They'll be managing the AI agents that do it for them.

Harvard Business Review put a name to this role in February: Agent Manager — accountable for making sure AI agents actually deliver results. Microsoft calls it the "agent boss" era — your value shifts from doing the task to setting intent and judgment.

Gartner predicts Fortune 500 companies will run 150,000 agents each by 2028, up from fewer than 15 in 2025. PwC's latest Global AI Jobs Barometer puts the AI-skills wage premium at 62% — up from 57% last year. And on Glassdoor, agent-orchestration roles start around $148,000 a year.

This isn't a someday problem — it's happening right now. Follow FOWL AI, Future of Work Lab, so you're the one managing the agents, not managed out by them.

posts.script:
AI agents are now coordinating with each other, delegating tasks, and delivering finished work — with no human in the loop. Here's what that actually looks like.

The U.S. Army is running an AI agent system, built by Salesforce, that already supports 9.2 million soldiers, veterans, and their families. Google's Agent2Agent protocol — the standard for agents talking to agents — is already live in production at Microsoft, AWS, and SAP. Anthropic built the same pattern into Claude: one lead agent delegates to specialist subagents working in parallel, then assembles their output into a finished result. And Gartner predicts 40% of new enterprise apps will ship with an agent built in by the end of this year.

There's a job title appearing in 2026 that most people have never heard of. By 2028, it could be as common as Product Manager.

It's called Agent Manager. In February, Harvard Business Review named and defined the role for the first time: "Just as product managers emerged during the software revolution, agent managers are becoming essential" now. Job boards are already listing it as "AI Agent Manager" — call it 2026's breakout title.

This isn't theoretical. At Salesforce, Zach Stauber's actual title is "support agent manager" — he manages a fleet of AI agents, reviewing their work, fixing exceptions, coaching them the way a manager walks the floor with a human team.

Postings for roles like this are up over 140% year over year. Average salary: around $103,000 — with senior roles pushing past $200,000.
